actions: Call on speakerphone immediately

Chest compressions 100–120/min, 5–6 cm; recoil
30:2 if trained/able, otherwise continuous compressions
AED prompts and dispatcher; keep clear for analysis/shock

routes.escalation: Emergency and CPR/AED until appropriate stopping condition or professional takeover.

routes.title: Paediatric arrest with regional algorithm intact

AHA infant technique heel of hand or two-thumb encircling; AED pediatric settings if available
avoid: Two-finger infant CPR promoted as current AHA
Withholding available AED solely for missing pediatric pads
routes.escalation: Immediate emergency service; dispatcher/local training precedence.

routes.title: Choking by effective cough and age

ERC/RCUK two-thumb infant thrust versus AHA heel-of-hand; dispatcher/local current training
Unresponsive: appropriate CPR pathway; visible object only

routes.escalation: Immediate help for severe obstruction; assessment after abdominal thrusts/chest compressions or persistent symptoms.

routes.title: Immediate danger: use local emergency dispatch
triggers: Severe breathing trouble, collapse, major injury, dangerous bleeding, severe allergic reaction, acute pregnancy emergency, or rapid deterioration
User asks which emergency hospital to select while unstable
minimum_context: Current physical location if known; if unknown, ask country/city while giving immediate action
Person's exact dispatch location should be shared with dispatcher
Current symptoms and immediate change, only enough to communicate urgency
actions: Say to call local emergency services now; give local-number example only when the country is verified
Tell caller to provide exact location first and follow dispatcher
Dispatcher chooses transport/destination based on condition and local system
A companion may check insurance or documents in parallel if it does not delay care
If already in clinician care, follow instructions and referral
avoid: Waiting for insurer approval, map search, photos, web translation, or records
Promising preferred hospital, language, or ambulance destination
routes.escalation: Immediate local emergency dispatch. Any worsening while waiting: update dispatcher and follow instructions.

routes.title: Find and verify appropriate local care
triggers: Stable non-life-threatening concern needing an appointment or same-day advice
User wants a nearby clinic, GP, pharmacy, diagnostic or specialty service
minimum_context: Country and current city/area or nearby landmark; ask permission before using location
Age group and pregnancy if relevant
Language, access needs, transport, walk-in/appointment preference
actions: Identify official health advice route/regulator/ministry/provider directory
Use maps/general search only to discover candidates
Confirm exact branch, service, hours, phone, eligibility, language and entrance on official branch source or verified call
Report evidence, timestamp, uncertainties, and next verification step
Escalate if symptoms worsen or fit emergency criteria
avoid: Use reviews/rating or tourism marketing as quality proxy
Invent capability, distance, cost, hours, or interpreter support
Collect unnecessary identifiers or medical records
routes.escalation: If danger signs emerge or uncertainty indicates possible emergency, call local emergency services. For unresolved stable uncertainty, use official local health advice line.

routes.title: Verify a specialty or time-sensitive capability
triggers: User asks for stroke, cardiac, paediatric, obstetric, imaging, dialysis, ICU or other specific capability
Search result claims a specialized centre
minimum_context: Exact needed service, age group, timing, referral requirements
Whether a clinician or dispatcher already recommended a destination
actions: For emergency, defer destination to dispatcher/local clinical system
For stable care, verify capability from official provider/regulator source and exact branch
Call verified facility contact where appropriate to confirm current operation and eligibility
Distinguish listed specialty from availability at this hour
avoid: Choose based on title, badge, reviews or hospital size alone
Claim live capacity from static directory
routes.escalation: Emergency condition: dispatch. Stable but service cannot be verified: call local health advice service or referring clinician.

routes.title: Travel insurance alongside necessary care
triggers: User asks whether insurance should be called first
Travel insurer, network, preauthorization, direct billing, or cost uncertainty
minimum_context: Destination and insurer/policy if voluntarily known
actions: Emergency: call dispatch first; companion may call insurer in parallel
Stable: use insurer's own policy/app/card contact
Ask about suitable facility, preauthorization, direct billing, deductible, exclusions, receipts and deadlines
Record reference and instructions if practical
State that policy and local practice determine coverage
avoid: Recommend unsuitable facility for network status
Assume EHIC/GHIC is global or covers repatriation
routes.escalation: Clinical urgency takes precedence; insurer follow-up can occur once immediate care is underway.

routes.title: Verify emergency number for current jurisdiction
triggers: User is abroad or has conflicting search results
minimum_context: Phone/network context if available without delay
actions: Use current official government/emergency-service source
Give number labeled with jurisdiction and checked date
Explain coverage limits and known conflicts
If immediate danger, ask nearby trusted person/local authority to call while user provides exact location
avoid: Give a global static number list
Test emergency number with a call
routes.escalation: Immediate danger: local emergency call; do not keep user waiting for research.

routes.title: Map listing conflicts with official facility information
triggers: Map says open but facility site says closed
minimum_context: Which source states each conflicting fact and its check time
actions: Show conflict instead of silently selecting one
Prefer responsible health authority and exact branch's own current source
For stable need, call verified official branch contact or health advice line
If emergency, use dispatch without waiting to settle map metadata
avoid: Treat map rating or edit as authoritative clinical information
Use old screenshots or an unrelated chain branch
routes.escalation: Emergency dispatch if urgent/deteriorating; otherwise official health line/provider confirmation.

routes.title: Language and communication support

minimum_context: Need for interpreter, hearing or communication access
actions: Emergency: call first; give exact location and plain symptoms
Offer a concise phrase to read/show in local language when useful
For stable care, verify interpreter/language access directly with official facility contact
Mark language as unconfirmed unless official source states it
avoid: Assume tourism-oriented English means clinical interpretation
Present machine translation as clinical diagnosis
routes.escalation: Emergency dispatch remains first; ask a trusted nearby helper to communicate if needed.

routes.title: Report verified facility candidates
triggers: User requests actual facility recommendations or comparison
minimum_context: Consent to use location; exact current area
Travel mode if distance is requested
actions: Provide exact facility and branch
Give address and distance only with stated origin/mode/source
State service fit with source-backed wording
Give hours/phone only when official source supports; mark unknown otherwise
Include source checked time and uncertainties
avoid: Rank by ratings, marketing, size, or proximity as clinical quality
Fabricate distance, availability, prices, coverage, appointment or capacity
Present search snippets as direct confirmation
routes.escalation: For danger signs, lead with emergency action and omit pre-call comparison.

routes.title: Possible endometriosis with stable symptoms
triggers: Disabling menstrual pain, chronic pelvic pain, deep sexual pain or cyclic bowel/urinary symptoms
Normal ultrasound with persistent clinically significant symptoms
Claim that laparoscopy is mandatory before any initial treatment
minimum_context: Age/life stage; symptoms, timing, severity and effect on daily life
Pregnancy possibility and urgent features before routine discussion
Relevant anatomy, previous imaging/operations and treatments when volunteered or clinically needed
actions: Explain a working clinical diagnosis and planned evaluation without diagnosing through chat. A normal routine ultrasound does not exclude superficial disease. S362 S364
Help prepare a symptom/impact summary, prior-treatment history and questions about appropriate ultrasound, specialist imaging and referral.
Present initial symptom treatment and investigation as potentially concurrent. Discuss alternatives rather than creating a mandatory invasive diagnostic ladder.
avoid: Declaring disease from a symptom checklist
Dismissing disease after one normal scan or normal examination
Using CA125, a classification stage or a symptom diary as a diagnostic test
Requiring an intolerable internal examination or assuming pregnancy intentions
escalation: Use the acute-pain route immediately for red flags.
Arrange clinical assessment for persistent symptoms, impaired daily function or treatment failure/intolerance; suspected deep disease or endometrioma warrants specialist discussion.

routes.title: New severe pain or possible pregnancy complication
triggers: Sudden severe or rapidly worsening pelvic/abdominal pain
Faintness/collapse, major bleeding, shoulder-tip pain with pregnancy possibility
Breathlessness/chest pain or severe illness despite an existing endometriosis label
minimum_context: Only information needed for immediate urgency: onset, severity, collapse/bleeding/breathing, pregnancy possibility and location for local help
actions: Prioritize emergency assessment when severe pain, collapse, significant bleeding or breathing difficulty is present. Do not wait to prove a relation to menstruation. S368
Mention urgent alternatives such as ectopic pregnancy, torsion, cyst complication or infection as reasons for assessment, without claiming a diagnosis.
If immediate danger is not apparent but fever, vomiting, urinary/stool blood or difficulty passing urine/stool is present, recommend prompt clinical triage.
Use any existing clinician-provided emergency plan as a separate established pathway; do not invent a prescription rescue regimen.
avoid: Calling the episode an endometriosis flare based only on history
Delaying urgent care for a photograph, pregnancy test result, symptom diary or extended questioning
Using pain relief or a negative biomarker to rule out an emergency
escalation: Emergency services/department for severe or unstable features; adapt contact details to the person's location.
Prompt clinician assessment for concerning but nonunstable associated symptoms.

routes.title: Possible deep urinary, bowel or extrapelvic disease
triggers: Cyclic dyschezia, hematuria, scar swelling or recurrent thoracic symptoms
Imaging suggests bowel, bladder or ureteral deep disease
minimum_context: Exact symptoms and scan/report wording, if available
Known obstruction, kidney function concerns or acute chest/breathing symptoms
Previous operations and relevant specialist involvement
actions: Explain that modest pain does not exclude significant ureteral obstruction and renal risk; suspected obstruction needs specialist organ assessment. S366
Discuss specialist imaging for anatomical mapping and multidisciplinary expertise, without converting an imaging label into an automatic operation. S365
Recognize extrapelvic patterns while retaining alternative diagnoses. S363
avoid: Reassurance based only on tolerable pain
Claim that all cyclic rectal/urinary bleeding is endometriosis
Providing bowel/ureter surgical technique instructions or a universal excision recommendation
escalation: Urgent specialist assessment for suspected obstruction or threatened organ function.
Emergency assessment for acute dyspnea, chest pain, severe abdominal pain, retention or other unstable features.

routes.title: Compare established pain and hormonal options
triggers: Request to compare nonhormonal, combined hormonal, progestin or GnRH approaches
Previous medicine inadequate or poorly tolerated
minimum_context: Main treatment goal and pregnancy intention
Exact prior/current products, use, response and adverse effects
Relevant thrombotic, migraine, liver, cancer, bone and mood history
actions: Distinguish no universal cure from meaningful symptom and functional benefit. S361
Explain class purposes, usual place in care, burdens and major safety categories; compare benefits with the person's stated goal.
Use method-specific contraindication assessment; estrogen contraindication does not make every hormonal method equivalent. S369
Explain add-back as a clinician-selected component with its own safety requirements; offer questions for a review rather than a personalized regimen.
Include multidisciplinary pain care and assessment of overlapping contributors when appropriate. S387
avoid: Choosing a prescription, dose, taper or add-back combination for the person
Promising lesion eradication, fertility improvement or permanent cure from pain treatment
Treating a progestogen endometriosis product as contraception without verifying its label
escalation: Clinician or specialist review for inadequate control, intolerance, complex contraindications or bone-affecting therapy.
Urgent help for severe mood deterioration or suicidal thoughts; emergency assessment for acute physical red flags.

routes.title: Verify a GnRH product, contraception and monitoring
triggers: Question about Orilissa, Yselty or a depot agonist
Assumption that a fibroid dose or another country's product label transfers directly
minimum_context: Exact brand, ingredients, route/formulation, market and current label
Contraception needs, co-medicines and relevant safety history
actions: Compare the precise jurisdiction-specific label and distinguish authorization, reimbursement and stock.
Identify US Myfembree nonhormonal contraception wording versus EU Ryeqo first-month and subsequent-use wording; do not blend them. S373 S374
Explain duration limits, bone monitoring, pregnancy and interaction issues at a category level; defer personal changes to the treating clinician.
State that the reviewed Yselty overview supports the endometriosis add-back indication but is not a complete SmPC check. S375
avoid: Self-directed conversion between products, depot formulations or add-back regimens
Declaring pregnancy impossible because bleeding stopped
Claiming Serbian/Russian approval without a verified local source
Presenting trial arms as automatically approved alternatives
escalation: Pharmacist/prescriber verification before applying conflicting instructions.
Prompt assessment for suspected pregnancy, major adverse effects or acute symptoms.

routes.title: Consider surgery or persistent postoperative symptoms
triggers: Request for excision or hysterectomy as a guaranteed cure
Pain persists or recurs after surgery
Proposed deep surgery or repeat endometrioma operation
minimum_context: Specific operative goal, lesion location, previous procedures and reports
Pain/organ/bleeding symptoms and change since surgery
Pregnancy plans, ovarian reserve concerns and current suppression
actions: Separate diagnostic, pain, organ-protection and fertility objectives.
Explain relevant organ complications, reserve effects and the possibility of persistent pain; specialist expertise matters. S366
Clarify that hysterectomy and ovary removal are separate decisions and neither guarantees removal of all pain contributors. S363
Discuss postoperative options and reassess overlapping pain causes; use PRE-EMPT without claiming one hormone universally prevents recurrence. S379
Flag the NICE/ESHRE difference about the objective of preoperative GnRH treatment instead of issuing a universal medication rule.
avoid: Guaranteeing cure from complete excision or hysterectomy
Assuming recurrence is the only cause of postoperative pain
Automatic repeat ovarian surgery based on size alone
Telling the person to start or stop prescribed preoperative hormones
escalation: Specialist review for deep disease, suspected organ compromise or repeated surgery.
Acute postoperative/severe new symptoms require urgent clinical assessment.

routes.title: Coordinate endometriosis care with fertility goals
triggers: Trying to conceive with suspected/confirmed endometriosis
Question about egg freezing, ovarian reserve or fertility benefit of suppression
minimum_context: Age, time trying and intended route to parenthood when relevant
Known tubal/ovulatory/semen factors and previous fertility care
Prior ovarian surgery, bilateral disease and available reserve assessment
Pain, suspicious imaging or organ risk that could create a separate indication
actions: Explain that pain-directed ovarian suppression does not improve pregnancy rates while attempting conception. S363
Present selected mild-disease surgical evidence with its narrow population and continuing-pregnancy outcome. S380
Avoid routine endometrioma surgery solely to improve ART live birth; discuss ovarian harm, pain and follicle-access exceptions with specialists.
Discuss fertility preservation as an option with uncertain eventual benefit, rather than a universal requirement or guarantee.
avoid: Predicting infertility from stage or a diagnosis alone
Treating AMH as a definitive natural-fertility forecast
Claiming deep surgery or repeated cystectomy always improves live birth
escalation: Fertility and endometriosis specialist coordination where surgery may compromise reserve or plans are time-sensitive.
Urgent organ/symptom pathway takes priority if red flags emerge.

routes.title: Adolescent, menopausal or gender-diverse presentation
triggers: Adolescent symptoms interfere with school or daily activity
Postmenopausal new pain, bleeding or mass
Trans man/nonbinary person with pelvic pain or prior hysterectomy
minimum_context: Life stage, relevant organs/surgeries and hormones only as clinically needed
Symptom pattern, examination preferences and consent
Urgent symptoms and pregnancy possibility without assumptions
actions: Take adolescent disabling or noncyclic symptoms seriously and discuss age-appropriate specialist care. S362
Do not transfer adult antagonist data to pediatric dosing; consider bone-development implications with specialists.
Evaluate new menopausal bleeding/mass for alternatives, including malignancy, rather than attributing it to previous endometriosis.
Use respectful anatomy-based reasoning and coordinate with existing gender-affirming or menopausal treatment; do not recommend abrupt hormone changes.
Explain the limited evidence behind menopausal regimen decisions and population-specific evidence gaps. S363
avoid: Assuming gender identity, lack of bleeding or hysterectomy rules out all endometriosis-related or other pelvic pathology
Inferring sexual activity, fertility intention or examination consent
Calling severe adolescent period pain normal by age alone
escalation: Prompt assessment for new postmenopausal bleeding/mass.
Specialist care for adolescent refractory symptoms; urgent route for severe pain or instability.

routes.title: Assess a novel drug, biomarker or AI claim
triggers: Dichloroacetate or AMY109 advertised as a cure
Saliva test described as perfect rule-out or general screening
AI accuracy presented as clinical utility
minimum_context: Intended clinical use, country and approval/funding claim
Study stage, comparator, population and relevant patient outcome
actions: Separate preclinical rationale, phase 1 safety, feasibility, diagnostic accuracy, clinical utility and authorization.
For EPiC1, explain the single-arm feasibility design, small sample and neuropathy; no DIY use or cure claim. S381
For AMY109, report the small phase 1 study and subsequent in-house development discontinuation; do not invent its cause. S382 S383
For saliva testing, report selected-population accuracy and imperfect negative predictive value; distinguish the French innovation pathway from universal endorsement. S384 S385
State access limitations and request a full protocol/regulatory source before making a stronger claim.
avoid: Equating a biomarker association or machine-learning score with a diagnosis
Converting small uncontrolled symptom changes into efficacy
Assuming a press release proves approval, access, cure or fertility safety
Using a negative test to dismiss urgent symptoms
escalation: Clinical evaluation continues according to symptoms and organ risk regardless of research-test enthusiasm.
Research participation discussion belongs with an authorized study team; no acquisition or self-dosing instructions.

routes.title: Map a new knowledge gap
triggers: A topic is requested but has no clear destination in the existing navigation graph
Maintainer asks what an existing topic or module covers
minimum_context: Whether the request is foundational education, evidence comparison, source discovery, patient-facing preparation, or system architecture
Known population and jurisdiction if clinical guidance is implicated
actions: Map the topic across anatomy/system, symptoms/conditions, tests, medicines, procedures/devices, population/life-stage, care setting, and urgency where relevant
Identify prerequisite concepts and adjacent topics; record explicit unknowns and missing current local sources
Use the existing navigation graph as entry/cross-link layer and add reference pointers as an overlay
Keep curriculum sources as learning-scope evidence and clinical guidelines as recommendation evidence
avoid: Claiming that topic presence or library size proves completeness or safety
Creating a parallel diagnostic decision tree or score engine
Using an unreviewed source inventory as evidence of clinical claims
escalation: If an urgent or safety-critical route has no verified current source and reviewed boundary, route to qualified care or an established emergency resource
If the request is asking for patient-specific diagnosis or treatment, use the applicable clinical-safety guidance rather than the architecture map

routes.title: Screen a source before adding it to a public knowledge set
triggers: A textbook, guideline, dataset, repository, lecture, or benchmark is proposed for reuse
A source is described as open or free but license scope is unclear
minimum_context: Exact title and URL or repository path
Intended action: link, read, quote, summarize, download, index, ingest, adapt, or redistribute
Source version and any third-party components
actions: Inspect exact publisher/title license and any AI-ingestion clause, exclusions, third-party credits, and jurisdictional terms
Record rights metadata independently from reading depth and clinical evidentiary value
For composite repositories, inspect per-file or per-dataset licenses and separately licensed software/content
When permission is unclear, retain only metadata and link to the source while seeking a rights review
avoid: Treating free access, a platform collection, an MIT code license, or a repository-wide label as permission for every asset
Reading or deriving from OpenStax textbook chapters under the stated no-AI-ingestion restriction without written permission
Ingesting ESC guideline content into AI/CDS based on public availability
Copying benchmark items or using a top-level repo license to override upstream licenses
escalation: Refer uncertain legal interpretation to qualified counsel or the rights holder
Do not add content to a retrieval index until the rights route is clear

routes.title: Create a provenance record for a clinical claim
triggers: A maintainer drafts, changes, or reviews a consequential health statement
minimum_context: Population, setting, jurisdiction, date/version, outcome, and decision context
Exact supporting source section and actual reading status
actions: Type the claim as mechanism, empirical finding, guideline recommendation, approval/status, availability, or uncertainty
Record study/guideline population, comparator/outcome, certainty/limitations, locator, source version, reviewer and date
Link credible disagreement, corrections, retractions, or superseding sources
Keep approval, recommendation, evidence, and availability fields independent
avoid: Treating a curriculum, regulator landing page, mechanism, trial registration, or abstract as proof of clinical efficacy
Claiming a full source was read when only metadata, abstract, table of contents, or search excerpt was seen
Silently replacing a source behind a stable reference
escalation: If a material claim has no applicable primary or authoritative support, label it unknown or remove it pending review
If patient-specific treatment is requested, keep the knowledge record separate from advice

routes.title: Review a source or recommendation after a change trigger
triggers: New guideline version, correction, retraction, regulator label, recall, major study, safety signal, local policy change, or rights change is detected
minimum_context: Old and new source versions or exact event
Affected claim IDs, populations, settings and jurisdictions
Date trigger was detected and reviewer
actions: Open the authoritative new version and inspect the relevant sections; record literal reading depth
Compare old/new recommendation, outcome, population, harms, certainty, product status and rights
Determine whether to add, narrow, supersede, withdraw, or leave a claim unchanged
Update affected navigation pointers and synthetic evaluations; preserve previous version and rationale
Prioritize event-driven review for safety alerts and high-impact topics; treat calendar intervals as queue planning only
avoid: Changing clinical content solely because the web page timestamp changed
Assuming newer automatically means better or applicable
Marking a source current because a fetch succeeded, when it was a login/error or an index excerpt
Automatically rewriting downstream guidance without review
escalation: For a possible serious safety alert or conflicting current guidance, pause unsupported claims and seek a qualified reviewer
If the authoritative source is inaccessible, record the access failure and do not claim review

routes.title: Retrieve a compact, applicable evidence bundle
triggers: A user asks for an explanation, evidence comparison, test meaning, treatment options, or source provenance
minimum_context: Relevant age/life-stage, jurisdiction, care setting, and exact product/route when they change the evidence
A clear statement of what remains unknown
actions: Resolve topic through existing navigation destinations, then retrieve sources attached to the best-matching claim
Prefer current applicable official guidance and regulator/label for practice/status; add systematic evidence or study for benefit/harms and a foundation source only for mechanism
Include credible competing guidance when relevant
Show close citations with exact title, version, section, population, jurisdiction and limitations
Say when only landing-page/abstract/index text was actually inspected
avoid: Searching broadly and mixing unrelated jurisdictions or populations
Returning many documents without explaining applicability
Filling a missing context gap by guessing
Treating tools or retrieval as a diagnosis
escalation: If urgent warning signs arise, stop ordinary retrieval and direct to emergency help under the reviewed emergency route
If exact label or local guidance cannot be verified, state that limit and direct the person to a pharmacist/clinician

routes.title: Explain treatment choices for clinician discussion
triggers: User asks what options are commonly discussed for a condition, how they compare, or what questions to ask a clinician
minimum_context: Known life-stage, exact product/formulation/route if raised, and what the user wants to understand
Whether the request asks for general options or an individualized decision
actions: Summarize guideline-supported options and evidence limits for the matching population
Describe likely benefits, harms, burdens, uncertainty, and patient preference factors in balanced terms
Separate established recommendations from newly issued guidance, authorized product status, investigational intervention, negative evidence, or discontinued product
Offer questions for a clinician and identify what local verification is needed
avoid: Selecting a treatment for the individual, prescribing, titrating, starting/stopping/tapering, or calculating renal/pediatric doses
Equating new, approved, available, guideline-supported, and effective
Changing insulin or blood-pressure treatment based on a bare number
escalation: Direct to the prescriber/pharmacist for a personal medicine change or product-specific question
If the question concerns a current emergency, use the reviewed emergency pathway

routes.title: Keep urgent pathways separate from ordinary knowledge retrieval
triggers: User mentions a possible emergency, rapid worsening, danger sign, or asks for immediate action
minimum_context: Only the minimum details needed to communicate urgency safely; do not delay emergency care to gather a complete history
actions: Use an independently reviewed urgent-care source and concise escalation language
Preserve the separate pathway for verified lay first aid and an already-prescribed rescue plan
For non-urgent continuation after safety is addressed, return to ordinary evidence discovery
avoid: Allowing missing data, source lookup, a photograph, a score, or an AI response to postpone emergency help
Giving medication changes from an isolated measurement
Turning a symptom matcher into a probability or diagnosis engine
escalation: When a potentially time-critical emergency is described, tell the user to contact local emergency services or seek immediate in-person care
Do not improvise first aid or rescue-plan directions; use only separately reviewed instructions

routes.title: Evaluate behavior across synthetic multi-turn cases
triggers: New route, source mapping, retrieval change, or user-facing behavior is proposed
minimum_context: Intended educational scope and forbidden behaviors
Synthetic fixture, expected criteria, applicable source keys, and version under review
actions: Test missing and contradictory context, updated sources, changes in age/jurisdiction/product, source access failure, and an urgent pivot
Check citation entailment, applicability, version, rights status, and whether limitations are reported
Test that the assistant asks only for context that changes the answer, abstains when unsupported, and does not cross into diagnosis or dosing
Review with qualified maintainers; monitor changes after release
avoid: Treating passing text checks, benchmark scores, volume of sources, or disclaimer presence as clinical validation
Using real patient records, transcripts, identifiers or genetics as public fixtures
Copying benchmark items or inferring a benchmark's license from repository-level code terms
escalation: If an evaluation reveals a safety-branch bypass or unsupported action, block that route until reviewed
If intended product use crosses into diagnosis, triage, or treatment, require a separate validation and regulatory workstream

routes.title: Find a foundational pharmacology learning section
triggers: The user asks for a plain-language explanation of pharmacokinetics, ADME, pharmacodynamics, or mechanism-of-action terminology
minimum_context: Whether the request is for a basic concept or a specific medicine/product decision
Audience and jurisdiction if the user asks for a professional education source
actions: Link to Open RN Nursing Pharmacology-2e sections 1.2 and 1.7 as US nursing-education resources
Label actual section titles, edition, CC BY 4.0 license with section-specific figure/third-party credits, and educational scope
For a product or treatment question, separately retrieve current exact product labeling and applicable guideline evidence
avoid: Treating foundation sections as efficacy, safety, approval, interaction, contraindication, or dose evidence
Implying that reading the textbook qualifies the user to administer or prescribe medicines
Copying chapter text, figures, learning activities, or answer keys without the required attribution and asset-level rights review
escalation: Route personal medicine changes or product safety questions to the prescriber or pharmacist and current local product information
If there is an urgent reaction or immediate danger, use the separately reviewed urgent-care route

routes.title: Use the CDC TB curriculum and course outline as learning-navigation sources
triggers: A clinician-education request concerns TB learning objectives or chapter organization
A maintainer needs an example of linking course outcomes to a subject map
minimum_context: Whether the request is about education or current clinical care
actions: Link the CDC Core Curriculum 7th edition and identify the inspected Chapter 1 sections and limits
Show the CE activity's objectives, target audience and expiration date; state that SS4444R expired 2025-03-19
For current practice questions, route to the current CDC TB guideline page and jurisdiction-specific TB program source
avoid: Calling the expired activity currently creditable
Treating course objectives or completion as proof of competence
Treating the 2021 manual as a substitute for current guidelines
Using course questions or copied figures as public evaluation data
escalation: For a patient-care TB question, use a current clinical guidance route and local public-health consultation where appropriate
For CE credit, verify the provider's current course catalog because the listed activity has expired

routes.title: Under-five fever with age-specific risk
actions: Assess whole child and trajectory
Suitable verified medicine only for distress
Five days or more: prompt clinical review
Under3m >=38 C or 3-6m >=39 C: urgent age-specific assessment; latest UK NHS urgent-help page directs emergency care
escalation: Emergency for altered responsiveness, severe breathing, abnormal colour or concerning rash/neck symptoms

routes.title: Barking cough and inspiratory noise
actions: Keep calm in comfortable position
Timely clinical advice
Explain clinician medicine/hospital care options without selecting regimen
avoid: Leftover steroid or nebulized adrenaline regimen
escalation: Emergency for major distress, drooling with unsafe swallow, exhaustion or altered responsiveness

routes.title: Bronchiolitis versus preschool wheeze
actions: Under-two bronchiolitis remains possible
Older/recurrent wheeze needs clinical differentiation
Help follow existing verified rescue plan and seek care
escalation: Emergency for severe/worsening breathing or poor response; urgent review for reduced intake/urine

routes.title: Seizure with fever
minimum_context: Existing rescue plan after initial actions
actions: Call for first/prolonged event
Time event, protect head, clear hazards
Monitor breathing; recovery position after event if normal breathing
Follow prescribed rescue plan when verified
escalation: Emergency ongoing first/prolonged event, abnormal breathing, focal or repeated events; first resolved event hospital assessment

routes.title: Vomiting/diarrhea and dehydration
actions: Urgent under-five dehydration assessment
Small regular appropriate ORS if alert and safe swallow
Exact packet dilution; usual feeds/food as tolerated
escalation: Emergency bilious/bloody vomit, severe pain, shock-like change or difficulty waking

routes.title: Ear pain and watchful waiting
actions: Explain examination-dependent diagnosis
Only clinician-agreed observation in eligible mild cases
Recheck if worsening/not improving
Explain antibiotic choices as clinician options
escalation: Prompt reassessment for drainage/high fever/worsening; emergency if child critically unwell

routes.title: Urinary symptoms or unexplained fever
actions: Prompt clinical assessment
Explain targeted sample/testing
Ask service about needed urine sample; deterioration must not wait for home collection
No self-ordered universal imaging package
escalation: Emergency for systemic deterioration or painful inability to urinate

routes.title: Limp, hot joint or refusal to use limb
minimum_context: Ability to bear weight without forcing
actions: Examine unexplained limp
Support and avoid forcing limb
Explain selected imaging/specialist referral
escalation: Emergency for refusal to bear weight, severe sudden pain, deformity, fever with illness or worsening

routes.title: Scrotal/testicular emergency
actions: Emergency assessment for sudden severe presentation
State torsion is time-sensitive without diagnosis
escalation: Emergency now for sudden severe pain or associated nausea/abdominal pain

routes.title: Pediatric product identity and error prevention
actions: Use exact label/pharmacist for suitability
No personalized dose calculation
Explain US under-two/manufacturer under-four versus UK under-six
Poison advice now for possible error
escalation: Emergency if collapse/seizure/abnormal breathing; otherwise urgent poison guidance for uncertain exposure

routes.title: Battery, magnets and poison
minimum_context: Swallowing and symptoms after initial routing
actions: Immediate care for battery/magnet even well
Poison service product/time context
Conditional NCPC honey protocol only if every condition verified
No emesis
avoid: Delay emergency travel to get honey
escalation: Emergency department immediately for battery/magnet; emergency services for collapse or airway compromise

routes.title: Toddler thermal/chemical/electrical burn
actions: Immediate thermal cooling under running water
Remove items unless stuck; loose covering after cooling
Follow EMERGENCY module and obtain child-specific advice
escalation: Emergency large/deep, face/genital, chemical/electrical or breathing concern

routes.title: Head injury and new symptoms
actions: Escalate warning signs
Urgent advice for vomiting/concerning change
After assessment follow supervision/discharge plan
escalation: Emergency for abnormal responsiveness, seizure, neurological change or major mechanism

routes.title: Water safety and submersion
actions: Incident: safe rescue, early call, EMERGENCY module
Prevention: designated attentive adult, barriers, life jackets
Lessons/lifeguard do not replace supervision
escalation: Emergency for unresponsiveness/abnormal breathing or deterioration after submersion

routes.title: Newborn/young-infant illness even afebrile
actions: Emergency danger signs before questions
Prompt age-specific examination even without fever
Explain clinician-selected tests and procedure purpose without a universal young-infant bundle or hospital protocol
escalation: Emergency abnormal breathing/response or deterioration; young-infant fever urgent clinical assessment, local stronger instructions apply

routes.title: Neonatal jaundice and age-hours interpretation
actions: Immediate assessment first24h
Timely bilirubin measurement/professional review
Persistent jaundice after2weeks: same-day clinical contact; prematurity context does not justify ignoring warning signs
Explain monitored phototherapy
avoid: Wait timing despite pale stools/dark urine
escalation: Emergency jaundice with poor feeding/response, abnormal breathing/temperature or first24h

routes.title: Infant reflux, feeding and hydration
actions: Stable effortless regurgitation supportive feeding advice
Flat back sleeping
Prompt clinical review feeding/growth concerns
Breast milk/formula central; avoid universal extra water
Professional rather than home acid-suppression/thickening plan
escalation: Emergency bilious vomit/danger signs; urgent projectile/bloody vomiting, feed refusal or dehydration

routes.title: Pediatric tests, reference intervals and vital observations
triggers: Adult range compared with neonatal result
actions: Use exact pediatric laboratory interval
Explain CALIPER scope without copying database
Bilirubin age-hours/gestation pathway
Discuss tests selected for management question
Visible distress overrides reassuring home oxygen
avoid: Routine chest X-ray for typical bronchiolitis
escalation: Clinical deterioration emergency regardless isolated lab/vital; other results interpreted with ordering clinician

routes.title: Age-specific surveillance and formal screening
actions: Distinguish surveillance, validated screening and diagnosis.
Use selected examples for appropriate age; do not recreate a scored questionnaire.
Identify local developmental assessment and early-support pathway.
escalation: Loss of skills or persistent concern: arrange pediatric assessment.
Sudden deterioration with acute illness: acute pathway.

routes.title: Corrected developmental age
actions: Explain chronological and corrected ages separately within first two years.
Use actual dates; discuss ongoing needs with treating team.
escalation: Persistent concerns or regression: pediatric assessment regardless of correction.

routes.title: Growth chart and measurement interpretation
actions: Check method and chart before comparison.
Explain WHO 0-5 scope and US WHO-to-CDC transition at 2.
Use serial accurate measurements and clinician context.
escalation: Poor intake, loss of weight or concerning trend: pediatric review.

routes.title: Adequacy and selective eating
actions: Prioritize adequate energy/fat and iron-rich foods.
Check actual alternative-drink labels.
Offer calm structured meals/snacks and repeated low-pressure exposure.
avoid: Precise energy target from incomplete diary
escalation: Deteriorating intake, painful swallowing, recurrent choking or growth concern: clinical/dietetic support.

routes.title: Food reaction and nutritional exclusions
actions: Distinguish immune allergy from intolerance without diagnosis.
Prepare pediatric/allergy assessment; protect nutritional adequacy.
Use emergency pathway and existing prescribed rescue plan if severe.
avoid: Home challenge after suspected serious reaction
escalation: Airway swelling, breathing difficulty, collapse or abnormal unresponsiveness: emergency help immediately.

routes.title: Safe food preparation below five
actions: Use alert upright seated supervised eating.
Quarter round foods; soften firm textures; remove bones and avoid coin shapes.
No whole nuts/popcorn below 5; no lumps of nut butter.
escalation: Active choking: first aid immediately; swallowing difficulty: professional assessment.

routes.title: Sleep, activity and screen age bands
actions: Distinguish age 1 screen recommendation from age 2 and 3-4.
Describe WHO activity and sleep totals with naps.
Offer realistic enjoyable change, not pressured regimen.
escalation: Persistent functional sleep concerns: pediatric discussion.

routes.title: Fluoride toothpaste and dental care
actions: Use smear below 3; pea from 3; adult help and twice-daily brushing.
State UK fluoride concentration guidance with local/dentist context.
Arrange dental review when not established.
avoid: Fluoride-free switch solely because cannot spit
escalation: Pain/swelling: dental assessment; severe associated symptoms: acute pathway.

routes.title: Speech, hearing and vision concerns
actions: Passed newborn hearing screen does not exclude later difficulty.
Ask for hearing assessment and relevant developmental support.
Explain AAPOS preschool age bands and professional testing; localize programme.
avoid: Home acuity score or patching prescription
escalation: Failed screen or persistent concerns: professional assessment; sudden deterioration: acute pathway.

routes.title: Supportive toileting and constipation
actions: Current NHS guidance does not require readiness signs before gentle learning.
Support foot position, easy clothing, calm routine and effort.
Check constipation before stopping nappies or increasing pressure.
escalation: Blood, vomiting, constant abdominal pain, bloating or weight loss: prompt assessment.
Persistent symptoms or difficulty: local pediatric support.

routes.title: Home safety and local well-visit navigation
actions: Briefly address water, batteries/magnets, medicines, falls and burn hazards.
Use actual national calendar/version and vaccination professional for reconciliation.
Prepare a focused appointment agenda; investigations need indication.
escalation: Actual ingestion/injury/drowning: acute pathway immediately.

routes.title: Newborn contact and examination plan
actions: Identify completed/outstanding procedures and responsible service.
Use England 72-hour/6-8-week examination as a localized example; obtain the actual local discharge/community-contact plan.
Cord care: gentle cleaning if soiled and drying; follow neonatal instructions.
escalation: New illness/feeding concern: acute infant assessment.

routes.title: Newborn screening results and repeats
actions: Explain screen versus confirmation.
Track every outstanding result and repeat separately.
Localize NHSday 5/results 6 w, hearing followup and USCCHD timing.
Prematurity/transfusion repeats belong to neonatal/screening team.
escalation: Positive/unclear screen: programme followup promptly; new acute symptoms override pass.

routes.title: Infant milk and formula safety
actions: Support feeding choices and qualified feed observation.
Use exact product ratio, measured water first, hygienic preparation and applicable 70 C mixing guidance.
No extra water/powder or additions.
Special formula/neonatal plans require professional instructions.
escalation: Poor intake or illness: infant clinical assessment.

routes.title: Complementary foods and safe allergen introduction
actions: Explain around 6 m readiness; milk continues.
Progress safe textures and iron-containing foods.
Introduce allergenic foods individually small amounts; continue tolerated foods.
escalation: Swallowing difficulty or known allergy: professional plan; severe reaction: acute emergency.

routes.title: Infant sleep and awake play
actions: Back sleeping on firm flat clear separate surface with room sharing.
No head-shape devices/pillows; skull concern routes separately.
WHO infant sleep groups and awake supervised tummy time; no pressure to force totals.
escalation: New breathing/responsiveness concern: acute emergency pathway.

routes.title: Current calendar, antigens and original blank planner
actions: Check current original calendar and amendments.
Use UKJuly 2026 cohort details as localized example.
Blank planner separates documented dose from planned appointment.
Vaccination service reconciles catchup and exact product contraindications.
escalation: Severe prior reaction/immunodeficiency: professional product assessment; acute severe reaction: emergency.

routes.title: Infant developmental observation at 2/4/6/9 months
actions: Use selected age-appropriate observation prompts.
Separate surveillance from standardized screening and diagnosis.
Consider corrected developmental age and progress across domains.
Arrange clinical review for missed skills, regression or persistent concern.
avoid: Prone sleep or pressured motor practice
escalation: Regression or persistent concern: pediatric assessment.
Sudden loss with acute illness: acute infant pathway.

routes.title: Outstanding screening result or transfer between services
actions: Distinguish sample collected from screening completed.
Identify who holds the result and who now owns follow-up.
Contact screening service for overdue result or pending repeat/referral.
Record completion, result and outstanding action separately in authorized private records only if requested.
avoid: Combine UK/US examples into universal calendar
escalation: Suspected positive/unclear result or requested repeat: prompt programme follow-up.
New symptoms override reassuring earlier screen.

routes.title: Ill infant or persistent tense fontanel
actions: Prompt medical assessment for a persistent tense/bulging fontanel while settled, even without other reported symptoms.
Emergency assessment for persistent tension with illness or neurological danger
Prompt assessment for under-three-month fever at least 38 C
Do not postpone for an image
avoid: Wait for photo or routine scan
routes.escalation: Emergency pathway when impaired responsiveness, seizure, abnormal breathing or severe illness.

routes.title: Closure timing in a well infant
actions: Explain variation and measurement method
Arrange examination when concern persists
Review growth and development
routes.escalation: Escalate for persistent abnormal shape, growth change or new illness.

routes.title: Changing head circumference
minimum_context: Chart, age, sex and prematurity reference
actions: Confirm professional measurement and consistent chart
Use local referral pathway
Prioritize neurological symptoms
routes.escalation: Urgent assessment for verified rapid change with neurological features.

routes.title: Pulsation or position-dependent prominence
minimum_context: Whether crying-related prominence resolves after settling
actions: Explain normal pulse possibility
Distinguish transient crying-related appearance from persistent abnormality
Provide reassessment trigger without a home clearance test
routes.escalation: Persistent tense bulge or illness routes urgently.

routes.title: Sunken appearance and intake
actions: Whole-child hydration assessment
Prompt clinical advice for poor intake/urine
Emergency assessment for severe illness
routes.escalation: Emergency if lethargic, abnormal breathing or shock concern.

routes.title: Flattening or positional preference
actions: Clinical assessment to distinguish positional shape and fusion
Safe-sleep-preserving awake positioning
Professional physiotherapy for restricted movement
routes.escalation: Early craniofacial referral for suspicious persistent shape or uncertain fusion.

routes.title: Forehead ridge
actions: Explain physiological ridge versus shape disorder
Recommend examination for narrowing or persistent concern
routes.escalation: Timely craniofacial review for triangular/narrow forehead or additional shape changes.

routes.title: Large or late-closing fontanel
actions: Pediatric review of whole pattern
Explain selected causes without assigning diagnosis
Targeted clinician-chosen tests
routes.escalation: Urgent route for neurological symptoms or severe illness; otherwise focused review.

routes.title: Vitamin D or calcium change request
triggers: stop vitamin D for small fontanel
minimum_context: Existing clinician plan and other supplements
actions: Do not derive treatment from gap size
Preserve verified plan pending clinician advice
Check duplicates and route suspected excess exposure
routes.escalation: Poison-service/clinical advice for suspected excess; emergency route if severely unwell.

routes.title: Scan choice or normal ultrasound claim
actions: Differentiate brain versus suture ultrasound
Explain indication-specific imaging
Do not delay specialist referral for extra local tests
routes.escalation: Urgency overrides elective imaging planning.

routes.title: Confirmed craniosynostosis options and follow-up
actions: Prepare questions about technique, window, risks and follow-up
Distinguish postoperative and cosmetic helmets
Reassess new symptoms after surgery
routes.escalation: Emergency for acute neurological danger; contact treating team for new postoperative concern.
